title: A Duck on the Pond
standard_text:

 Spiral: RI.K.2 main topic · RI.K.4 unknown words · RI.K.7 illustrations · RI.K.10 group reading
 Lower range: LL 0 – 110

paras.label: A
paras.text: A duck has soft feathers under its wings.

paras.label: B
paras.text: Oil on the top feathers keeps the water out.

paras.label: C
paras.text: The soft ones under them stay dry.

paras.label: D
paras.text: So the duck stays warm all day long.

paras.label: A
paras.text: A duck has soft feathers under its wings.

paras.label: B
paras.text: Oil on top keeps the water out.

paras.label: C
paras.text: The soft ones stay dry.

paras.label: D
paras.text: The duck stays warm.

questions.q: What keeps the water out?
questions.a: Oil on the top feathers keeps the water out.

questions.q: Paragraph C (i.e. the soft feathers) and paragraph D (i.e. staying warm).
Tell what this is about.
questions.a: A duck has soft feathers under its wings. Oil on the top feathers keeps the water out, so the soft ones stay dry and the duck stays warm.

questions.q:
feathers: what covers a bird.
oil: a slippery stuff that water runs off.
Describe the connection between the oil and the duck staying warm.
questions.a: Oil on the top feathers keeps the water out, so the soft ones under them stay dry and the duck stays warm.

note: Read it twice. The second time, stop after each paragraph and ask what that one sentence told you.

title: The Crossing Light

 Lower range: LL 0 – 110

paras.label: D
paras.text: Look both ways even when the man is white.

paras.label: A
paras.text: A white man means you may cross.

paras.label: B
paras.text: A red hand means wait.

paras.label: C
paras.text: Numbers count down the seconds.

paras.label: D
paras.text: Always look both ways too.

questions.q: What does the red hand mean?
questions.a: A red hand means you must wait.

questions.q: Paragraph C (i.e. the numbers) and paragraph D (i.e. looking both ways).
Tell what the crossing light shows.
questions.a: A white walking man means you may cross and a red hand means you must wait. The numbers count down the seconds left, and you look both ways even when the man is white.

questions.q:
cross: to walk from one side to the other.
count down: to go backward, like five, four, three.
Describe the connection between the white man and looking both ways.
questions.a: You look both ways even when the man is white, because the light tells cars to stop but cannot make them.

note: Paragraph D is the one that matters most and it comes last. Say it again at the end.

paras.label: D

questions.q: Where does the bear sleep?
questions.a: A bear finds a cave or a hole in winter.

questions.q: Paragraph C (i.e. not eating) and paragraph D (i.e. spring).
Tell what a bear does in winter.
questions.a: A bear finds a cave or a hole, sleeps there for many months without eating, and comes out thin and hungry in spring.

questions.q:

spring: the season that comes after winter.

note: Four paragraphs, four steps, in order. Count them on your fingers with the child.

questions.a: She keeps bandages, ice packs and a cot.

questions.q: Paragraph C (i.e. writing it down) and paragraph D (i.e. calling home).

questions.a: The nurse has a small room by the office with bandages, ice packs and a cot. She writes down every child who comes in, and she calls home if a child needs to go.

note: Children know this room. Ask what they have seen in it before you read a word.

paras.label: D
paras.text: A coat of fur comes and goes with the year.

paras.label: A

paras.label: B

paras.label: C
paras.text: In spring the dog sheds it.

paras.label: D
paras.text: The fur comes and goes.

questions.q: What does the thick fur hold?
questions.a: The thick fur holds warm air near the skin.

questions.q: Paragraph A (i.e. growing fur) and paragraph C (i.e. shedding it).
Tell what this is about.
questions.a: A dog grows thicker fur when it gets cold, and the thick fur holds warm air near the skin. In spring the dog sheds it, so a coat of fur comes and goes with the year.

fur: the hair that covers an animal.
sheds: drops off.
Describe the connection between the cold and the thick fur.
questions.a: A dog grows thicker fur when it gets cold, and sheds it again in spring.

note: The topic is the whole year, not just winter. Paragraph D is what says so.

freezes: turns into ice.

questions.q:

breathe: to take in air.
Describe the connection between the rain and the worms on the path.
questions.a: When it rains hard the tunnels fill with water, so the worms come up so they can breathe and you see them on the path.

note: Go out after rain and look. The child will have the answer before you read a word.

block: to get in the way of.

questions.a: At noon the sun is high and the shadow is short, so the shadow moves and changes all day as the sun moves.

note: Chalk around a shadow in the morning and look again at lunch. The text is the explanation.

count: to say how many.

paras.text: Hatch means to come out of an egg.

paras.label: C
paras.text: The chick pecks the shell.

paras.label: D
paras.text: Nobody helps it.

questions.q: What does hatch mean?
questions.a: Hatch means to come out of an egg.

questions.q: Paragraph C (i.e. pecking) and paragraph D (i.e. no help).
Tell what hatch means.
questions.a: The book says the chick will hatch today. Hatch means to come out of an egg, the chick pecks the shell from inside, and it takes many hours and nobody helps it.

questions.q:
hatch: to come out of an egg.
pecks: hits with a beak.
Describe the connection between pecking and hatching.
questions.a: The chick pecks the shell from inside, which is how it comes out of the egg.

note: Paragraph D is the hard part to hear. Children want to help, and the text says not to.

questions.a: Line up means to stand one behind another.

questions.q: Paragraph C (i.e. the space) and paragraph D (i.e. not bumping).

space: the gap between two things.
Describe the connection between the space and not bumping.
questions.a: You leave a little space in front of you, so then the line can walk without bumping.

paras.text: The sign says the tulips will bloom in April.

paras.text: Bloom means to open into a flower.

paras.label: C
paras.text: Before that the bud is closed and green.

paras.label: D

paras.label: A
paras.text: The sign says the tulips will bloom.

paras.label: B
paras.text: Bloom means to open into a flower.

paras.label: C
paras.text: First the bud is closed and green.

paras.label: D
paras.text: Then the petals show their color.

questions.q: What does bloom mean?
questions.a: Bloom means to open into a flower.

questions.q: Paragraph C (i.e. the closed bud) and paragraph D (i.e. the petals).
Tell what bloom means.
questions.a: The sign says the tulips will bloom in April. Bloom means to open into a flower, before that the bud is closed and green, and after it blooms the petals show their color.

questions.q:
bloom: to open into a flower.
bud: a closed flower before it opens.
Describe the connection between the bud and the petals.
questions.a: Before it blooms the bud is closed and green, and after it blooms the petals show their color.

note: Before and after is the shape here. Ask which paragraph is before and which is after.

title: The Front of a Book
standard_text:
Standard: Identify the front cover, back cover, and title page of a book.
 Spiral: RI.K.4 unknown words · RI.K.6 author and illustrator · RI.K.7 illustrations · RI.K.10 group reading
 Lower range: LL 0 – 110

paras.label: A
paras.text: The front cover is the first thing you see.

paras.label: B
paras.text: It has the name of the book on it.

paras.label: C
paras.text: It usually has a big picture too.

paras.label: D
paras.text: The front cover tells you what is inside.

paras.label: A
paras.text: The front cover is what you see first.

paras.label: B
paras.text: It has the name of the book.

paras.label: C
paras.text: It has a big picture.

paras.label: D
paras.text: It tells you what is inside.

questions.q: What is on the front cover?
questions.a: It has the name of the book on it.

questions.q: Paragraph C (i.e. the picture) and paragraph D (i.e. what is inside).
Tell what the front cover does.
questions.a: The front cover is the first thing you see. It has the name of the book and usually a big picture, and it tells you what is inside.

questions.q:
cover: the outside of a book.
name: what a thing is called.
Describe the connection between the picture and what is inside.
questions.a: The front cover usually has a big picture, and the front cover tells you what is inside.

note: Hold a real book. Point at the front cover before you say anything about it.

paras.label: D

paras.label: A
paras.text: Turn the book over to find the back.

paras.label: B
paras.text: The back tells a little about the story.

paras.label: C
paras.text: It can have words from readers.

paras.label: D
paras.text: The price is in a corner.

questions.q: What does the back cover tell you?
questions.a: The back often tells you a little about the story.

questions.q: Paragraph C (i.e. words from readers) and paragraph D (i.e. the price).
Tell what the back cover has on it.
questions.a: Turn the book over to find the back cover. It often tells you a little about the story, it can have stars or words from readers, and the price is usually printed in a corner.

questions.q:
back cover: the outside at the end of a book.
price: how much something costs.
Describe the connection between the front cover and the back cover.
questions.a: The front cover is the first thing you see, and you turn the book over to find the back cover.

note: Front and back as a pair. Have the child flip a book over and name each one.

title: The Title Page
standard_text:
Standard: Identify the front cover, back cover, and title page of a book.
 Spiral: RI.K.4 unknown words · RI.K.6 author and illustrator · RI.K.7 illustrations · RI.K.10 group reading

paras.label: A
paras.text: Open the cover and turn one or two pages.

paras.label: B
paras.text: The title page says the name of the book again.

paras.label: C
paras.text: It also says who wrote it and who drew it.

paras.label: D
paras.text: The front cover is outside and this page is inside.

paras.label: A
paras.text: Open the cover and turn a page.

paras.label: B
paras.text: The title page says the name again.

paras.label: C
paras.text: It says who wrote it and who drew it.

paras.label: D
paras.text: The cover is outside and this is inside.

questions.q: What does the title page say?
questions.a: The title page says the name of the book again.

questions.q: Paragraph C (i.e. who wrote and drew it) and paragraph D (i.e. inside and outside).
Tell what the title page is.
questions.a: Open the cover and turn one or two pages to find the title page. It says the name of the book again and who wrote it and who drew it. The front cover is outside and the title page is inside.

questions.q:
title: the name of a book.
title page: the page inside that gives the name again.
Describe the connection between the front cover and the title page.
questions.a: The front cover is outside and this page is inside, and both of them say the name of the book.

note: The repeat confuses children. Say plainly that the name appears twice on purpose.

title: Which Way Is Up
standard_text:
Standard: Identify the front cover, back cover, and title page of a book.
 Spiral: RI.K.4 unknown words · RI.K.6 author and illustrator · RI.K.7 illustrations · RI.K.10 group reading
 Lower range: LL 0 – 110

paras.label: A
paras.text: A book has a top and a bottom.

paras.label: B
paras.text: The words go the right way up when you hold it right.

paras.label: C
paras.text: The spine stays on your left as you read.

paras.label: D
paras.text: Turn pages from the right to the left.

paras.label: A
paras.text: A book has a top and a bottom.

paras.label: B
paras.text: Hold it so the words are the right way up.

paras.label: C
paras.text: The spine stays on your left.

paras.label: D
paras.text: Turn pages right to left.

questions.q: Where does the spine stay?
questions.a: The spine stays on your left as you read.

questions.q: Paragraph B (i.e. the words the right way up) and paragraph D (i.e. turning pages).
Tell how to hold a book.
questions.a: A book has a top and a bottom. You hold it so the words go the right way up, the spine stays on your left as you read, and you turn pages from the right to the left.

questions.q:
spine: the folded edge where a book is held together.
turn: to move a page over.
Describe the connection between the spine and turning pages.
questions.a: The spine stays on your left as you read, so you turn pages from the right to the left.

note: Do it with them rather than telling them. Hand over a book upside down and wait.

paras.label: D

paras.label: A
paras.text: The spine is the folded edge.

paras.label: B
paras.text: It holds the pages together.

paras.label: C
paras.text: The name is printed on it.

paras.label: D
paras.text: That is how you find it on a shelf.

questions.q: What does the spine hold?
questions.a: It holds all the pages together.

questions.q: Paragraph C (i.e. the printed name) and paragraph D (i.e. finding it on a shelf).
Tell what the spine of a book is.
questions.a: The spine is the folded edge of a book. It holds all the pages together, the name is printed down the spine, and that is how you find a book on a shelf.

questions.q:
spine: the folded edge that holds a book together.
shelf: a flat board that holds books.
Describe the connection between the name on the spine and finding a book.
questions.a: The name is printed down the spine, and that is how you find a book on a shelf.

note: Stand a book on a shelf and ask what you can still see. Only the spine.
